capitals.name: Teotihuacan
capitals.note: Infobox 'Built 100 BCE - 250 CE', 'Abandoned 750 CE'. Coordinates from the project gazetteer's place entry.

correction.text: the city 'thought to have been established around 100 BCE' (infobox 'Built 100 BCE - 250 CE'; 'Period I occurred between 200 – 1 BCE')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Teotihuacan at -50; the page founds the city c. 100 BCE. Drawn as the city and its immediate hinterland only; the ledger's -50 event carries the growth to Cliopatria's first shape.

Redrawn (review fix 1). Cliopatria's first shape (5,674 km2, 20 grid cells, bbox -98.99..-98.02, 18.86..19.70) is not 'the eastern Basin of Mexico around the city': it lies in the Puebla-Tlaxcala valley, 7 cells in México state, 5 in Tlaxcala and 8 in Puebla; its centroid (polities.csv -98.51, 19.295) is about 55 km SSE of the city; the capital (19.69 N, 98.84 W) is about 11 km outside it and only 1 of the 3 cells of the dossier's own 15 km city circle is inside; and it contains 5 of the 7 cells of Cholula's circle and both cells of Cacaxtla's core. No page opened puts Cholula or Cacaxtla under Teotihuacan (Teotihuacan page: 'other nearby centers, such as Cholula, Xochicalco, and Cacaxtla, competed to fill the power void'; Cholula page: 'a major center contemporaneous with Teotihuacan', and it is not called a tributary, ally or dependent), so no vassal events are recorded. Replaced by a 40 km radius around the city (16 cells, about 4,700 km2 on the grid against Cliopatria's 5,674 km2: the same order of size, centred on the city, no cell shared with Cholula or Cacaxtla). The radius is the researcher's reading; the page gives no territorial extent. No infobox area to compare: the UNESCO zone is 3,381.71 ha and the city 'covered twenty-one square kilometres'. The -50 date is Cliopatria's; the page is silent on when the city came to control its valley (ledger -50, confidence 1). Years -50..105.

correction.text: the city and the valley around it, years -50..105: 'approximately half all people in the Valley of Mexico' lived in the city at its height and '80 to 90 percent of the total population of the valley resided in Teotihuacan'
same 40 km shape around the city as teotihuacan_-50; years 106..199 only. After Cuicuilco's abandonment c. 150-200 CE the whole Basin of Mexico passes to Teotihuacan (new keyframe teotihuacan_200).

keyframe_review.note: Years and place. Cliopatria's 106 shape is the same Puebla-Tlaxcala shape as the -50 one (see teotihuacan_-50), so it is redrawn the same way; the years 106..199 stand. Cuicuilco 'seems to have been abandoned around AD 150 to 200 after the eruption of a nearby volcano, Xitle', its people dispersing 'toward Toluca and Teotihuacan' (re-read: 'This disaster led to the dispersion of Cuicuilca culture towards Toluca and Teotihuacan').

correction.text: the center of the Basin of Mexico after Cuicuilco's abandonment: 'This series of eruptions gave rise to Teotihuacan as the center of the Basin of Mexico' (Cuicuilco page)

keyframe_review.note: Redrawn (review fix 2). The first version was Cliopatria's 106 shape united with the gazetteer region 'Valley of Mexico', which is all of México state plus the Distrito Federal (81 cells, west to 100.43 W, the whole Toluca valley inside): 94 cells against Cliopatria's 20, with no page giving that extent. The Cuicuilco page sends Cuicuilco's people 'towards Toluca and Teotihuacan', which keeps Toluca separate. Replaced by a 60 km radius around the city (40 cells, bbox -99.30..-98.34, 19.16..20.18, about twice Cliopatria's 5,674 km2; no cell shared with the Cholula or Cacaxtla circles; the Cuicuilco cell at 19.29 N, 99.18 W is inside). The page gives no territorial extent for the state; the basin is the researcher's reading of 'The city reached its peak in 450 CE when it was the center of a powerful culture' (Teotihuacan page), with 150,000 people (one estimate 250,000), once its only rival in the basin was gone ('The most prominent of these appears to have been Cuicuilco'). The sphere beyond the basin (Tikal 378-426) is carried by vassal events, not by this shape. The monuments were 'sacked and systematically burned around 550 CE'; the shape is kept to 649 because the page dates the decline to 600-700 and Period IV from 650.

Years and place (review fixes 1 and 3). Cliopatria's 656 shape is the same Puebla-Tlaxcala shape as the -50 one and is redrawn the same way. The keyframe now starts in 650, the page's 'Period IV describes the time period between 650 and 750 CE', so years 650..655 are no longer without a shape (the 200..649 keyframe ended in 649 and Cliopatria's shape began in 656); 'the city started to decline between 600 and 700 CE'. The ledger's 650 loss explains the shrink from the 60 km shape.

correction.text: unchanged shape (the 40 km shape around the city of teotihuacan_-50); years 650..691: 'Period IV describes the time period between 650 and 750 CE'

keyframe_review.note: Same shape, 692..704. Cliopatria's 692 shape is the same Puebla-Tlaxcala shape and is redrawn like the -50 one. Cliopatria ends the row in 704; the infobox gives 'Abandoned 750 CE', so the new keyframe teotihuacan_705 carries the declining city to 750; the ledger's 705 loss (confidence 1) explains the shrink.

correction.text: unchanged shape (the 40 km shape around the city of teotihuacan_-50); years 692..704
the declining city only: 'Period IV describes the time period between 650 and 750 CE'; infobox 'Abandoned 750 CE'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the last decades, city and hinterland only. 'The city may have lasted until sometime between the 7th and 8th centuries CE'.

region.text: The city is thought to have been established around 100 BCE

ledger.note: 100 BCE: Teotihuacan is established in the northeastern Basin of Mexico. 'The city is thought to have been established around 100 BCE'; infobox 'Built 100 BCE - 250 CE'; 'Period I occurred between 200 – 1 BCE'; 'The first human establishment in the Teotihuacan area dates back to 600 BCE'. The year is the page's rounded estimate, the 15 km core the researcher's.

region.text: the valley around the city (Cliopatria's first shape, redrawn): the city's 40 km neighbourhood without the founding core

ledger.note: 50 BCE: Teotihuacan comes to dominate the valley around the city (Cliopatria's first keyframe, redrawn around the city). The page is silent on the date of territorial control: it gives 'Period I occurred between 200 - 1 BCE and marks the development of a distinctively urban area', 'In the Tzacualli phase (c. 1-150 CE), Teotihuacan saw a population growth to approximately 60,000 to 80,000 people' (newcomers mostly from the basin), the Pyramid of the Sun 'completed by 100 CE' and 'c. 200 CE, the urban population had reached its maximum'. The Teotihuacan Mapping Project page, tried for a date of the city's growth into its hinterland, could not be read (URL not found, twice). Bridging event at confidence 1.

region.text: the southern and western Basin of Mexico around Cuicuilco: 'This series of eruptions gave rise to Teotihuacan as the center of the Basin of Mexico'

ledger.note: c. 150–200: Cuicuilco is abandoned after Xitle's eruption and its people disperse 'toward Toluca and Teotihuacan'. The Cuicuilco page's dates conflict (infobox 'Abandoned: 2nd–3rd century CE'; destruction 'sometime between 245 and 315 CE'; the Teotihuacan page puts Xitle 'roughly around 100 BCE'); 200 is the end of the page's 'around AD 150 to 200'. Cuicuilco (an urban centre from c. 150 BCE, peak 20,000) has no Cliopatria row; flagged for a dossier. The land is now the 60 km radius minus the 40 km core (review fix 2), not the whole 'Valley of Mexico' region: the Cuicuilco page says 'This series of eruptions gave rise to Teotihuacan as the center of the Basin of Mexico' and sends the Cuicuilca 'towards Toluca and Teotihuacan'.

region.text: Tikal and Uaxactun in the Petén: Siyaj K'ak' 'exerted control over other cities, including Uaxactun, where he became king'

ledger.note: 378: Siyaj K'ak' arrives at Tikal and a Teotihuacan-backed dynasty takes the throne. Chak Tok Ich'aak 'was killed on 14 January 378 AD', the day Siyaj K'ak' arrived from the west; Yax Nuun Ahiin I, 'the son of Spearthrower Owl', who 'may even have been the ruler of Teotihuacan', was enthroned on 13 September 379. Drawn as the lighter vassal tint (Teotihuacan's sphere), not as territory; whether the influx came 'via peaceful interaction or military invasion is still being very actively debated' (Siyaj K'ak' page). The mayan-city-states dossier should carry the matching relation.

region.text: Tikal and Uaxactun in the Petén: Siyaj K'ak' 'exerted control over other cities, including Uaxactun, where he became king'

ledger.note: c. 426 (bridging): the Teotihuacan-installed line at Tikal is 'rapidly Mayanized' ('Although the new rulers of Tikal were foreign, their descendants were rapidly Mayanized'). The Tikal page says Yax Nuun Ahiin I 'reigned for 47 years as king of Tikal, and remained a vassal of Siyaj K'ak' for as long as the latter lived', which gives 379 + 47 = 426 as the latest end; Siyaj K'ak' 'remained a power in the region until his death early in the fifth century' (Siyaj K'ak' page). The Yax Nuun Ahiin I page conflicts: infobox 'Died: 17 June 404 Tikal' but 'It is unclear when Yax Nuun Ahiin I died', his son Siyaj Chan K'awiil II 'enthroned in November 411', and accession 12 September 379 (the Tikal page says 13 September). The end is therefore somewhere between 404 and 426 and no page states it; 426 is kept as the Tikal page's upper bound at confidence 1. 'By the 7th century, there was no active Teotihuacan presence at any Maya site'.

region.text: the Basin of Mexico beyond the city's core

ledger.note: 650: Teotihuacan's hold on the Basin of Mexico lapses as Period IV begins. 'Period IV describes the time period between 650 and 750 CE'; 'the city started to decline between 600 and 700 CE'; its 'major monuments were sacked and systematically burned around 550 CE'. The year is the page's period boundary, the land the researcher's reading: the 60 km shape of 200..649 shrinks to the 40 km core, and the redrawn 650..691 keyframe now starts in the same year (Cliopatria's own shrink is in 656).

region.text: the valley around the declining city, leaving 'the city' only

ledger.note: 705: the city's neighbourhood falls away and only the city itself is drawn to its end. Cliopatria ends the row in 704; the page dates Period IV to 650-750 CE and the decline to 600-700 CE, but gives no year for the shrink to the city alone. Bridging event at confidence 1 so that the 705..750 keyframe (the city only) follows from the ledger.

750: Teotihuacan is abandoned. Infobox 'Abandoned: 750 CE'; 'The city may have lasted until sometime between the 7th and 8th centuries CE'; 'Its collapse might be related to the extreme weather events of 535–536'. Cliopatria ends the row in 704. The Epiclassic centres Xochicalco (founded c. 650) and Cacaxtla (650–900) rose after the fall; the basin itself had no state until 'During the 1200s CE, Nahua migrants repopulated the area'.

wars.name: Teotihuacan entrada at Tikal

zones.text: Tikal, El Perú and Uaxactun in the Petén

wars.outcome: Siyaj K'ak', 'probably a foreign general', arrives at Tikal on 14 January 378 as Chak Tok Ich'aak dies; Yax Nuun Ahiin I, son of Spearthrower Owl, is enthroned on 13 September 379 and Siyaj K'ak' becomes king at Uaxactun. Tikal is drawn as Teotihuacan's client 378–426.
wars.note: Not a contest zone: the page records a change of dynasty, not years of fighting over ground. 'Via peaceful interaction or military invasion is still being very actively debated' (Siyaj K'ak' page).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines: the basin frontier is the researcher's reading of the page; the Petén sphere is a client relation, not a border.

sources.title: Kaminaljuyu
sources.note: Thin: Teotihuacan-style vessels in the Esperanza tombs, no dates; re-read for the repair, still no years for any Teotihuacan connection and no statement of control; no event drawn.

sources.title: Matacapan
sources.note: Thin: location in the Tuxtlas near Catemaco (18.5 N, 95.233 W), no dates; no event drawn.

sources.title: Yax Nuun Ahiin I
sources.note: Repair: accession 12 September 379, infobox death 17 June 404 but 'unclear when ... died', successor Siyaj Chan K'awiil II enthroned November 411; conflicts with the Tikal page's 47-year reign (ledger 426, now confidence 1).

notes: Cliopatria's single row -50..704 is one state (the city of Teotihuacan), not successive states; kept as one dossier with the start moved to -100 and the end to 750 on the page's dates. Teotihuacan's sphere: the orchestrator asked for the reach beyond the valley 'as a sphere rather than territory'; it is drawn here as vassal events (the lighter tint) inside this dossier, not as a separate slug. Only Tikal (378–426) could be dated from the pages opened; Kaminaljuyú ('elite-use ceramic vessels in unmistakable Teotihuacán style' in Esperanza tombs, undated), Matacapan (its page has no dates), Copán ('In 426, the Copán ruling dynasty was created' by Yax K'uk' Mo', not described as a client) and Monte Albán (the Oaxaca barrio, undated) stay out of the ledger: a gap-filler with the Kaminaljuyú Esperanza phase or Matacapan literature could add vassal events c. 400–550. Disagreement: Xitle's eruption is 'roughly around 100 BCE' on the Teotihuacan page but 245–315 CE (destruction) and 'around AD 150 to 200' (abandonment) on the Cuicuilco page; the 200 gain follows the Cuicuilco page. Cuicuilco needs a small dossier (no Cliopatria row). The 'Valley of Mexico' gazetteer region (81 cells, about 20,500 km2) is broader than the hydrological basin and took in the Toluca valley; it is no longer used (see the repair paragraph). Pages opened: 6 against a budget of 5; Kaminaljuyu and Matacapan were thin and carry no event. The Seshat page for mx_basin_of_mexico_7 was not tried after seshat-db.com refused the Monte Albán polity page. REPAIR 2026-10-18 (reviewer's fail, three fixes applied): (1) Cliopatria's shapes -50, 106, 656 and 692 are one Puebla-Tlaxcala shape (20 cells: 7 in México, 5 in Tlaxcala, 8 in Puebla; centroid about 55 km SSE of the city; the capital about 11 km outside; it holds Cholula's capital cell and Cacaxtla's core), so all four are marked adjust and redrawn as a 40 km radius around the city (16 cells). Re-read: the Teotihuacan page says 'other nearby centers, such as Cholula, Xochicalco, and Cacaxtla, competed to fill the power void' and the Cholula page calls it 'a major center contemporaneous with Teotihuacan' without making it a dependency, so no vassal events were added in either dossier. (2) The 200..649 keyframe is a 60 km radius (40 cells) instead of 'Valley of Mexico', with the Cuicuilco page's 'center of the Basin of Mexico'; ledger 200 and 650 follow. (3) The 650..655 gap is closed: the 650..691 keyframe starts at the page's Period IV; a bridging 705 loss (confidence 1) explains the shrink to the city alone. Thin items: the Teotihuacan Mapping Project page could not be read (URL not found, twice), so the -50 date stays Cliopatria's at confidence 1 (the Teotihuacan page dates the city's population growth to the Tzacualli phase c. 1-150 CE but not its control of the valley); the Yax Nuun Ahiin I page conflicts with the Tikal page on the end of the Tikal relation (404 infobox, successor enthroned 411, against 379 + 47 = 426), so the 426 vassal_end is now confidence 1; the Kaminaljuyu page re-read gives no years for any Teotihuacan connection, so the sphere beyond Tikal still has no dated events.
